target_customer: Developers of RNA and DNA medicines and vaccines (biotech and pharma licensees)
problem: RNA and gene medicines trigger an overactive innate immune response in cells, which limits tolerability and effectiveness.
business_model: Platform technology developer; expected licensing and partnering of its RNAx tolerability platform (not stated as live revenue)

founders.name: Thomas Folliard
founders.background_notes: YC page lists him as founder; the PR Newswire release calls him CEO and co-founder. No background in sources I opened.

founders.name: Barbara Mertins
founders.background_notes: Named co-founder in the August 2023 PR Newswire release; not on the YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Engineering how cells respond to RNA and lipid nanoparticles is research-grade biology that needs lab work and years before clinical use.

defensibility.rationale: A patent application exists (EPO publication seen in search results) and the platform is a specific encoded protein, but it is early and unproven in humans.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No acquirer or copycat found in the sources I opened.

market_need_then: In 2019 the company described a need for full-length human proteins for drug discovery; by 2023 the pitch was reduced immune reactions to RNA medicines, after the large scale use of mRNA vaccines.

brand_strength.rationale: Almost no public brand presence beyond a minimal site and one 2023 stealth exit release; no evidence the name helps or hurts.

pivots.from: Engineered human cell line to produce full-length human proteins for drug discovery (per a Fierce Biotech 2019 headline seen in search results; article itself blocked)
pivots.to: RNAx, an encoded protein that dampens immune response to RNA and LNP medicines

outcome_analysis: Excepgen is a very small biotech that stayed quiet after YC and surfaced in August 2023 with a $4M seed that took reported total seed funding to $14M, led by RA Capital. It is still alive but the product has moved from protein production to RNA tolerability, and no clinical or commercial result is public yet.
notes: Company says total seed funding is $14M after the $4M round of August 2023, so about $10M of earlier money is undated and unitemized (SeedTable lists a $9M July 2020 seed, single aggregator, unverified). CB Insights shows $4.15M total, which conflicts. Fierce Biotech fetch was blocked (403). No dated competitor source found near the 2019 batch, so the list is empty. No shutdown, sale or layoff found.
